info.title: Premierlytics API
info.description: Fantasy Premier League data. Authenticat with a publishable key (pk_) from the browser or a secret key (sk_) server side.

get.description:
Separate from /health deliberately.

/health answers "is the process alive" which is the right
check for a load balancer, and it must not fail because a
database is briefly unreachable.

/health/db answers "can we server requests", which is what
monitoring should alert on.

get.description:
The gameweek in progress: the most recent deadline that has passed.

Distinct from /next, and both exist simultaneously between a deadline and
the last whistle. A live-scores view wants this one; a transfer planner
wants the other.
The next deadline. What a transfer planner needs.

By season-scoped player_id.

Note this is NOT stable across seasons — FPL reassigns element IDs each
August, and id 3 has belonged to three different people in three seasons.
For a player's history, resolve player_code first.

schema.title: Response List Fixtures V1 Fixtures Get

get.description:
match_id is a slug: 25-26-prem-everton-vs-liverpool.

Globally unique — it encodes season and competition — so no season
parameter is needed.

match_id.title: Match Id
match_id.description: Globally unique identifier, and a readable slug rather than a number: `25-26-prem-everton-vs-liverpool`. It encodes season and competition, so no season parameter is needed to resolve one.

gameweek.title: Gameweek
gameweek.description: FPL gameweek, 1-38. Null for fixtures not assigned to one — some cup and European ties. Note that pre-season friendlies ARE assigned numbered gameweeks rather than gameweek 0, so filter on `competition` rather than assuming a gameweek implies a league match.

competition.title: Competition
competition.description: Which competition. `prem` for the Premier League; also `champions-league`, `europa-league`, `conference-league`, `efl-cup`, `community-shield`, `uefa-super-cup` and `friendly`. 2026/27 contains 97 friendlies — filter on this for anything scoring-related.

kickoff_utc.title: Kickoff Utc
kickoff_utc.description: Kickoff time, UTC. Null where upstream has not published one: unscheduled knockout ties, and every league fixture in 2025/26 gameweeks 34-38, which carry results but no timestamp. See the data quality page.

home_team_code.title: Home Team Code
home_team_code.description: Stable club identifier — survives across seasons, unlike `team_id`. Always populated: a fixture with no Premier League home side does not appear here.

home_team_name.title: Home Team Name
home_team_name.description: Display name for the season in question. Not stable — 'Ipswich' in 2024/25 became 'Ipswich Town' in 2026/27, same club, same code. Group by `home_team_code`, not by name.

away_team_code.title: Away Team Code
away_team_code.description: Stable club identifier for the away side. **Null means the opposition is not a Premier League club** — a European or cup tie against a foreign or lower-league side. That is information rather than missing data.

away_team_name.title: Away Team Name
away_team_name.description: Display name for the away side. Null for non-league opposition.

home_score.title: Home Score
home_score.description: Goals scored by the home side. Null if the fixture has not been played.

away_score.title: Away Score
away_score.description: Goals scored by the away side. Null if the fixture has not been played.

home_elo.title: Home Elo
home_elo.description: ClubElo rating for the home side **at kickoff**, not an end-of-season figure. Being point-in-time, it carries no hindsight and is safe as a model prior — including for promoted clubs, whose rating derives from their Championship form and so exists before they have played a top-flight match. Null for fixtures not yet played, and for non-league opposition.

away_elo.title: Away Elo
away_elo.description: ClubElo rating for the away side at kickoff. See `home_elo`.

Fixture.title: Fixture
Fixture.description:
A single match, from the home side's perspective.

Underlying storage is per team per match — two rows per fixture — because
almost everything at team level is asymmetric. This collapses that to one
row with the natural home/away orientation.

One consequence: European away ties where the home side is not a Premier
League club have no row here, since we hold no identity for the opposition.
A team's full schedule across all competitions is available per team
rather than per fixture.

deadline_utc.title: Deadline Utc
deadline_utc.description: Transfer deadline, UTC — roughly 90 minutes before the first kickoff. Teams lock at this instant, so it is the cutoff for any information a manager could have acted on. Verified against an independent epoch field on every build, so a timezone misparse cannot go unnoticed.

is_finished.title: Is Finished
is_finished.description: Whether every fixture in the gameweek has been played.

is_data_checked.title: Is Data Checked
is_data_checked.description: Whether FPL has finalised scoring for the gameweek. Bonus points are provisional until this is true, and points can still change.

fixture_count.title: Fixture Count
fixture_count.description: League matches in this gameweek. **Not always 10.** Rounds get rescheduled around cup and European commitments, so 7 and 13 both occur legitimately in a normal season. A count above 10 usually means fixtures were moved into this week; below, moved out.

first_kickoff.title: First Kickoff
first_kickoff.description: Earliest league kickoff. Null where no fixture carries a time.

last_kickoff.title: Last Kickoff
last_kickoff.description: Latest league kickoff. The gameweek is not settled until this match ends, which is the relevant window for anything live.

average_score.title: Average Score
average_score.description: Mean score across all FPL managers. Null until the gameweek is played. Useful as a baseline: beating the average is the minimum bar for a strategy to be worth anything.

highest_score.title: Highest Score
highest_score.description: Best single-manager score in the gameweek.

most_selected_player_id.title: Most Selected Player Id
most_selected_player_id.description: Most-owned player at the deadline, as a season-scoped `player_id`. Resolve via `/v1/players/{player_id}` with the same season — this id is reassigned each August and is not comparable across seasons.

most_captained_player_id.title: Most Captained Player Id
most_captained_player_id.description: Most-captained player, season-scoped `player_id`. Captaincy is a stronger ownership signal than selection, since it is a single concentrated bet rather than a squad slot.

transfers_made.title: Transfers Made
transfers_made.description: Total transfers made by all managers ahead of this gameweek.

has_usable_snapshot.title: Has Usable Snapshot
has_usable_snapshot.description:
Whether a point-in-time capture exists close enough to this deadline to be meaningful.

Before a gameweek, false is expected — there is nothing to capture yet. **After one, false means the capture missed**, and any feature built for that gameweek is unreliable. Published rather than hidden because a silently stale snapshot is worse than an obviously absent one.

snapshot_at.title: Snapshot At
snapshot_at.description: When the authoritative capture for this deadline was taken. Always strictly before `deadline_utc` — a capture at the deadline instant is already too late.

hours_before_deadline.title: Hours Before Deadline
hours_before_deadline.description:
How stale the snapshot was. Captures run every three hours, tightening to every fifteen minutes in the six hours before a deadline, so a healthy value is **under 0.25**.

Larger means the cadence did not hold for that gameweek. The data is real but staler than intended, and injury news in particular moves fast enough that three hours matters.

Gameweek.title: Gameweek
Gameweek.description:
One FPL gameweek: its deadline, its fixtures, and how it turned out.

The deadline is the field everything else hangs off. It is the instant
teams lock, and it is the boundary that makes a feature either legitimate
or leaked.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Season-scoped identifier. **Reassigned every August** — id 3 has belonged to three different people across three seasons. Fine for requests within one season; joining on it across seasons blends careers and returns no error.

player_code.title: Player Code
player_code.description: Permanent identifier. The same human keeps it year to year, so this is the correct key for any historical query, career aggregate, or cross-season join.

team_code.title: Team Code
team_code.description: Stable club identifier — survives across seasons, unlike `team_id`. Fixture data joins on this.

team_name.title: Team Name
team_name.description: Club name for this season. Not stable across seasons: 'Ipswich' became 'Ipswich Town', same club, same code. Group by `team_code`.

web_name.title: Web Name
web_name.description: Short display name, as FPL shows it. Not unique — two players at the same club can share one.

position.title: Position
position.description:
`GKP`, `DEF`, `MID` or `FWD`. Determines scoring: goal values, clean sheet eligibility, and the defensive contribution threshold all vary by position.

Null for 20 players in 2024/25 whose position the source recorded as unknown — all of whom played zero minutes.

price.title: Price
price.description:
Current price in millions, from the most recent capture. Only meaningful for the season in progress; for a finished season it is whatever was true when we last captured.

Prices move nightly. For the price at a specific deadline, use the snapshot endpoints rather than this field.

selected_by_percent.title: Selected By Percent
selected_by_percent.description: Share of FPL managers owning this player, as a percentage. Current, not point-in-time.

status.title: Status
status.description: Availability flag. `a` available, `d` doubtful, `i` injured, `s` suspended, `u` unavailable, `n` not in squad. Current state, so it reflects today rather than any past gameweek.

news.title: News
news.description:
Free-text injury or availability note from FPL. Null when there is nothing to report — which is the common case and means the player is presumed fit.

This field moves faster than any other: a press conference on Friday can change it hours before a deadline. It is the main reason captures tighten to every fifteen minutes before one. Absent entirely for 2024/25, where the source did not carry it.

chance_of_playing_next.title: Chance Of Playing Next
chance_of_playing_next.description: FPL's stated percentage chance of featuring in the next gameweek, 0-100. **Null means no flag** — the player is presumed available — rather than unknown.

ep_next.title: Ep Next
ep_next.description:
FPL's own expected points projection for the next gameweek. Useful as a baseline: any model worth running should beat it on rank correlation.

Flat before a season starts — every player shows the same value until matches have been played, so it carries no signal in the opening weeks.

state_as_of.title: State As Of
state_as_of.description: When the capture behind the current-state fields was taken. If this is hours old, so are the price and news above it.

appearances.title: Appearances
appearances.description: League matches with at least one minute played. Excludes European and cup fixtures.

assists.title: Assists
assists.description: League assists, using FPL's definition — which differs from the conventional football one and changed for the 2025/26 season.

xg.title: Xg
xg.description: Expected goals across league matches. A measure of chance quality rather than outcome, so it is more stable week to week than goals and generally a better predictor of future scoring.

points.title: Points
points.description:
Total FPL points this season.

Derived from per-match data, which is missing roughly 2% of scoring events, so this will not always equal FPL's official figure exactly. Indicative for display; see the data quality page before relying on it for anything precise.

bonus.title: Bonus
bonus.description: Bonus points awarded, on top of the base points already included in `points`.

Player.title: Player
Player.description:
One player in one season.

Three blocks, and they answer different questions:

- **Identity** — who this is, and which of the two identifiers to use.
- **Current state** — price, ownership, availability. What is true *now*,
  from the most recent capture.
- **Season totals** — what has happened so far, derived from per-match
  data.

The current-state block is the wrong source for historical features. It
reflects today even for gameweeks long finished, so building a model on it
means training on information nobody had at the time. Use the
snapshot-scoped endpoints for that.

total.title: Total
total.description: Total matching the filters, ignoring pagination. Use it to decide whether more pages exist.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Rows skipped. Add `limit` to fetch the next page.

PlayerPage.title: PlayerPage
PlayerPage.description:
A page of players.

Offset pagination rather than cursor: a season has under a thousand
players and the set is stable within one, so offsets do not shift
underneath a paging client.

team_code.title: Team Code
team_code.description: Permanent club identifier. Survives across seasons and through relegation, so it is the correct key for anything historical. Fixture data joins on this rather than `team_id`.

team_id.title: Team Id
team_id.description: Season-scoped identifier, 1-20, assigned alphabetically each August. Reassigned as clubs are promoted and relegated, so it is not comparable across seasons.

team_name.title: Team Name
team_name.description: Club name as FPL renders it for this season. **Not stable** — 'Ipswich' in 2024/25 became 'Ipswich Town' in 2026/27, same club, same code. Grouping by name splits one club in two.

strength.title: Strength
strength.description: FPL's overall strength rating on a 1-5 scale. Coarse, and set by FPL rather than derived from results — but it is what their own fixture difficulty ratings are built from, so it is worth having when comparing against `ep_next`.

strength_overall_home.title: Strength Overall Home
strength_overall_home.description: FPL's home strength rating, on a larger scale than `strength` — typically 1000-1400. Higher is stronger.

strength_overall_away.title: Strength Overall Away
strength_overall_away.description: FPL's away strength rating. Usually lower than the home figure.

latest_elo.title: Latest Elo
latest_elo.description:
ClubElo rating after this club's most recent completed match. A current-strength figure, suitable for display or comparison.

For modelling, use the per-fixture `home_elo` and `away_elo` on the fixtures endpoint instead — those are the rating **at kickoff** and carry no hindsight, whereas this one reflects everything that has happened since.

latest_match_at.title: Latest Match At
latest_match_at.description: Kickoff of the match `latest_elo` reflects. Null before a club has played, or where that fixture carries no timestamp.

matches_played.title: Matches Played
matches_played.description: League matches played. **Null rather than zero before a season starts**, so a club yet to play is distinguishable from one that has played and lost everything. Excludes European and cup fixtures.

wins.title: Wins
wins.description: League wins. Null before the season starts.

draws.title: Draws
draws.description: League draws. Null before the season starts.

losses.title: Losses
losses.description: League defeats. Null before the season starts.

goals_for.title: Goals For
goals_for.description: League goals scored. Null before the season starts.

goals_against.title: Goals Against
goals_against.description: League goals conceded. Null before the season starts.

goal_difference.title: Goal Difference
goal_difference.description: `goals_for` minus `goals_against`. Null before the season starts.

Team.title: Team
Team.description:
One club in one season.

Season-scoped because clubs are: strength ratings change, the numeric id
is reassigned, and even the name is not stable. `team_code` is the only
thing that survives.

Two independent measures of strength are carried. FPL's own ratings drive
its fixture difficulty display; ClubElo is a rating system computed from
results. They disagree often, and the disagreement is sometimes the
interesting part.
